description: Inspect a residential service entrance and grounding electrode system for code violations. Verify proper grounding electrode installation, bonding connections, conductor sizing, and system grounding integrity.
environmentDescription: A residential utility room and exterior service entrance showing the grounding electrode system, service panel, water pipe bonding, and ground rods.

violations.description: Ground rod not meeting minimum 8-foot length requirement

citations.text: A ground rod needs a length of at least 8 feet and a diameter of at least 5/8 inch (1/2 inch is allowed for listed stainless or nonferrous rods).
A manufactured grounding electrode is normally two rods, each 3 m long, driven in full length, spaced at least 3 m apart and bonded together.
citations.description: Ground rod shorter than the 3 m rod length
citations.hintText: A manufactured ground electrode uses 3 m rods driven in full length. Check the rod length.
citations.inspectionNote: This ground rod is only 6 feet (about 1.8 m) long, shorter than the 3 m rods the code expects.

violations.hintText: Ground rods must be at least 8 feet long and 5/8 inch diameter. Check the rod length.
violations.inspectionNote: This ground rod is only 6 feet long, failing to meet the 8-foot minimum required by code.

violations.description: Grounding electrode conductor not connected to service equipment

citations.text: The grounding electrode conductor is the link between the grounding electrode(s) and the service's equipment grounding conductors and enclosures and, if the system is grounded, its grounded conductor.
The earthing conductor runs from the main earthing terminal to the earth electrode or the supplier's earth terminal and must be connected at the main earthing terminal.
citations.description: Earthing conductor not connected to the main earthing terminal
citations.hintText: The earthing conductor must connect the main earthing terminal to the earth electrode or the supplier's earth terminal. Look for a disconnected or missing conductor.
citations.inspectionNote: The earthing conductor is disconnected at the main earthing terminal. No path to earth exists.

violations.hintText: The grounding electrode conductor must connect from the panel to the grounding electrode. Look for a disconnected or missing conductor.
violations.inspectionNote: Grounding electrode conductor is disconnected at the service panel. No path to earth exists.

violations.description: Metal water piping not bonded to grounding system

citations.text: Bond the metal water pipe system to any one of these: the service enclosure, the service's grounded conductor, a grounding electrode conductor of adequate size, or the electrodes in use.
Bond the building's metal water piping to the electrical grounding system with a bonding conductor.
Extraneous metal that enters the building, such as a metal water service pipe, is bonded to the main earthing terminal.
citations.description: Metal water service pipe not main-bonded to the earthing terminal
citations.hintText: Look for a main bonding clamp and conductor on the water pipe near where it enters the building.
citations.inspectionNote: The metal water service pipe enters the building without a main protective bonding conductor to the main earthing terminal.

violations.hintText: Metal water pipes must be bonded to the grounding system. Look for a bonding clamp and conductor.
violations.inspectionNote: Metal water pipe enters the building without a bonding connection to the electrical grounding system.

violations.description: Equipment grounding conductor undersized for circuit

citations.text: Wire-type equipment grounding conductors are at least the size Table 250.122 specifies.
Size the circuit protective conductor (cpc) for the fault energy, or from the line conductor size, so it can carry a fault safely.
citations.description: Circuit protective conductor undersized for the circuit
citations.hintText: The cpc is sized for the fault energy or from the line conductor size, not just for the protective device rating.
citations.inspectionNote: The circuit protective conductor is too small for the circuit it serves.

violations.hintText: Equipment grounding conductors must be sized per Table 250.122 based on the overcurrent device rating.
violations.inspectionNote: Equipment grounding conductor is 14 AWG on a 30A circuit. Table 250.122 requires minimum 10 AWG for 30A.

violations.description: Multiple grounding electrodes present but not bonded together

citations.text: Bond together every electrode of the types listed in 250.52(A)(1) through (A)(7) at a building so they act as one system.
Connect together all the grounding electrodes at a building so that they act as one grounding system.

violations.hintText: All grounding electrodes at a building must be bonded together into one system.
violations.inspectionNote: Ground rod and water pipe electrode are both present but not bonded together. They must form a single grounding electrode system.

violations.description: Electrical system grounding does not limit voltage from lightning or surges

citations.text: Grounding a system ties it to earth to hold down surge voltages (from lightning, line surges, or an accidental touch of higher-voltage lines) and to keep voltage to earth stable during normal use.

violations.hintText: The system ground must provide a low-impedance path to earth for lightning and surge protection.
violations.inspectionNote: Service grounding connection uses a corroded clamp with high resistance, failing to provide adequate surge protection.

violations.description: Bare aluminum grounding electrode conductor in contact with earth

citations.text: Aluminum grounding electrode conductors, whether bare or copper-clad, are off limits where they would touch masonry or soil directly or sit in a corrosive environment.

violations.hintText: Aluminum grounding electrode conductors cannot contact masonry or earth directly.
violations.inspectionNote: Bare aluminum grounding electrode conductor is run through earth to the ground rod. Aluminum corrodes in contact with soil.

violations.description: Water pipe electrode not meeting 10-foot earth contact requirement

citations.text: A metal underground water pipe counts as an electrode only when 10 feet or more of it touches the earth, including bonded metal well casing in contact with earth.

violations.hintText: To qualify as a grounding electrode, a metal water pipe must have at least 10 feet of earth contact.
violations.inspectionNote: Metal water pipe transitions to plastic 4 feet after entering the building. Less than 10 feet of metal is in contact with earth, so it does not qualify as a grounding electrode on its own.

violations.description: Missing intersystem bonding termination for communications grounding

citations.text: Provide an intersystem bonding termination outside enclosures at the service or meter enclosure, and at the disconnect of any additional building or structure.

violations.hintText: An intersystem bonding termination is required for communications (cable, phone, antenna) grounding.
violations.inspectionNote: No intersystem bonding termination is provided at the service equipment for communications system grounding connections.

violations.description: Single ground rod used as sole electrode without supplemental electrode

citations.text: When the only electrode is one rod, pipe or plate, add a second electrode and bond it to the first, to the grounding electrode conductor, to the incoming grounded conductor at the service, or to the service enclosure.

violations.hintText: A single ground rod must be supplemented by an additional electrode unless it can achieve 25 ohms or less.
violations.inspectionNote: Only one ground rod is installed with no supplemental electrode. Unless resistance is verified at 25 ohms or less, a second rod is required.

violations.description: The {term:grounding} electrode conductor to the {term:ground-rod} is joined midway with a wire nut

citations.text: The conductor to an electrode runs in one unbroken length. Where a splice is needed, only irreversible compression connectors or exothermic welds are allowed for wire-type conductors; wire nuts and split bolts are not.

violations.hintText: Follow the conductor from the {term:panel} to the rod. Is it one piece the whole way?
violations.inspectionNote: Midway along the bare copper conductor to the {term:ground-rod}, two lengths are twisted together inside a yellow wire nut. No compression sleeve or weld mark is visible.
